paragraphs: For the next performance, the designer asked volunteers to find the running time and the interval without reading the plot. She noted where they hesitated, not simply whether they liked the new cover. One heading still caused confusion because it used a term familiar to staff but not to several visitors. She changed the wording and checked it with another small group.

The test did not prove that every reader would find everything immediately. It did give the theater a clearer reason for the next change. Staff also kept a note of which details had been moved, so that an essential item would not disappear during a later update. The space on the page was useful when it helped readers choose where to look. Keeping that purpose in view mattered more than removing words for its own sake.
rationale: 間接疑問・関係節・否定・動名詞を読み、文挿入の照応と利用者の問いに合う編集を理解する。

paragraphs: Before storing the box again, the club asked two younger members to use the notes to explain a comparison. They could identify the winning sail, but one note did not say whether the fan had stayed in the same position. Without that detail, the distance figures were difficult to compare fairly. The original makers added what they could confirm and marked what they could no longer check. They did not create a precise record from an uncertain memory. The younger members suggested a clearer form for the next project, with space for the test setup as well as the result. This gave the earlier work another use: it showed which information a future experiment needed to collect. The box preserved both useful findings and the limits of the evidence, leaving room for a better investigation rather than presenting the project as finished forever.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・不定詞を読み、記憶依存の問題と実験条件を記録する意味を理解する。

paragraphs: Before the next issue, the group checked when the entrance information had last been confirmed. A route that worked on a quiet morning might be harder to use when stalls moved during a busy event. The editor added a date and a contact point for questions, rather than promising that one photograph showed every possible condition. She also invited comments from readers whose needs the group had not yet considered.

One reader asked about places to rest, a detail absent from the first revision. The volunteers checked this and added a short note without replacing the rest of the article. Their aim was not to claim that the selection was complete. It was to make useful information easier to find and to show how readers could raise another question. A welcoming article could remain open to correction while still giving practical help.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・不定詞・比較を読み、文挿入の必要性と利用案内を更新する条件を理解する。

paragraphs: A month later, staff reviewed whether the new arrangement had made the reports easier to act on. Some cards described a problem clearly, but did not identify the item. Staff added a simple equipment number and placed matching numbers on the return cards. They also explained where an item would wait until inspection was complete. A report did not automatically mean that the equipment was safe to lend again. The person checking it recorded the decision and the date, so the next shift could see its status. Users were still asked only to describe what they noticed, not to make that decision themselves. The center kept a few examples of unclear reports for staff training without naming the users. Improving the return system meant connecting an observation to a particular object and then to a recorded response, rather than collecting more cards without a clear next step.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・受動態・動名詞を読み、報告と点検判断を分けて引き継ぐ仕組みを理解する。

paragraphs: After the sale, the students compared the questions buyers had asked with the information on each tag. Some wanted a lighter garment, while others cared more about repair or adjustment. The club did not turn these preferences into one new ranking of all clothes. Instead, it kept separate notes on condition and possible uses so that the next description could be more specific.

The students also marked repairs they had only suggested rather than actually completed. A possible improvement was not the same as the item's present state. They checked the wording with the volunteer before the next sale. Clearer descriptions could help buyers choose, but did not guarantee that every garment would suit every person. The work of setting a price now included explaining the basis of a judgment and leaving room for a buyer to value a different feature.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・比較・動名詞を読み、記述の照応と現状・修理可能性・個人の価値判断の違いを理解する。
